content.mission: Protect and save lives, minimise property damage and return the Changi aerodrome quickly to normal safe operations: provide aircraft rescue and firefighting, manage the Airport Emergency Plan and take charge of rescue, firefighting and crash-site operations.

sequence.label: Arrive
sequence.action: Respond to the scene of an aircraft accident at the aerodrome within 2 minutes, not exceeding 3 minutes.

sequence.label: Fire control
sequence.action: Bring the aircraft fire under control within a minute of arrival.

sequence.label: Rescue
sequence.action: Follow fire control swiftly with rescue, and evacuate casualties to nearby medical facilities.

sequence.label: Airport Emergency Plan
sequence.action: Manage the Airport Emergency Plan, coordinating the mutual aid agencies within the airport and its immediate vicinity, and take charge of rescue, firefighting and other crash-site operations.

sequence.label: Command posts
sequence.action: Direct the overall response from the crisis management operations centre, with a mobile command post moved to the site for local coordination.

sequence.label: Crash at sea
sequence.action: For an aircraft incident in the waters around the airport, respond with the sea rescue capability and coordinate with specialist rescue services.

sequence.label: Other emergencies
sequence.action: Respond to dangerous goods incidents, bomb warnings and chemical or biological threats within the airport.

hand_offs.when: Law and order and aviation security at the airport are involved, including an act of unlawful interference.
A bomb warning or suspected explosive device is confirmed.
The emergency becomes a major disaster or civil emergency, or extends beyond the airport and its vicinity.
Casualties are evacuated to medical facilities.

good_looks_like.description: First rescue and firefighting vehicles at the aircraft accident within 3 minutes
Aircraft fire reported under control within a minute of arrival

standards.source: ANR-139 (S 10/2023); AIP Singapore AD 2 WSSS; CAG
key_points: The aerodrome operator must provide rescue and firefighting services whose level of protection and response time comply with the Aviation Specifications.
Rescue and firefighting personnel must be trained, including live fire drills, and readily available to ride the vehicles.
The emergency plan must coordinate the response at the aerodrome or in its vicinity and be tested through emergency exercises.
Changi is Category 10 for rescue and firefighting on all three runways.
CAG states a response of 2 minutes, not exceeding 3, and fire control within a minute of arrival.
standards.decision_thresholds: Arrive within 3 minutes; fire under control within 1 minute of arrival.

workflow.endgame: Fire out, casualties evacuated to medical facilities, and the aerodrome returned to normal safe operations.

legal_authorities.power: The aerodrome operator must keep an emergency plan that coordinates the response at the aerodrome or in its vicinity, including specialist rescue services for water, and test it through exercises.
The aerodrome operator must provide rescue and firefighting services at the required level of protection and response time, with trained personnel readily available.
The aerodrome operator must provide a crisis management operations centre for overall direction and a mobile command post for local coordination at the site.

review.notes: Site-specific doctrine, approved by the user on 22 Nov 2026 as an exception to WS9 6.19. Scope: aircraft accidents at Changi aerodrome and its vicinity. An aircraft_impact into a building away from the airport is SCDF's (sg_scdf.*). Time targets are CAG's own published targets. No public source states when command passes from AES to SCDF, or what SPF does at a crash site; those hand-off triggers are Assumed. Equipment and vessels named in the sources are not transcribed.
